bug_semantics: A remote ActivityPub Create/Note can supply an Emoji tag whose icon.url and name are attacker-controlled. NodeBB converted a matching shortcode into an img element by interpolating those values into quoted HTML attributes after the original note content had already been sanitized, then stored the generated HTML. Remote-post rendering could bypass markdown/sanitize-html, so an attribute breakout in the generated markup became persistent same-origin JavaScript for viewers.
flaw_origin: Commit 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 introduced incoming ActivityPub emoji expansion in src/posts/create.js before database storage and first wrote the causal unescaped sink, interpolating tag.icon.url directly into img src. Commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 added the unescaped title attribute from tag.name one day later. Commit 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3 later moved/generalized the existing mechanism as Helpers.renderEmoji; it is a refactor, not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names author and committer Julian Lam <julian@nodebb.org>, contains only the message 'feat: #12683, parse incoming emoji tags and replace in content prior to storage in database', has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and uses no bot identity.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/NodeBB/NodeBB/issues/14601 documents the remote inbox -> notes.assert -> posts create path, sanitization-before-renderEmoji ordering, storage, and remote display bypass; GHSA-fh4m-97qj-ff6c and CVE-2026-73038 identify versions before 4.15.0 and reference c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e. `git log -S 'Rewrite emoji references to inline image assets' -- src/posts/create.js` identifies 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 and shows it adding the tag.icon.url interpolation before db.setObject. `git show 4ba41a68011c7151925bfcbf3ab6168e97c9d893:src/posts/create.js` directly verifies that the immediate parent has no emoji-tag rewrite or generated img sink. `git log -S 'title="${tag.name}"' -- src/posts/create.js` identifies 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 as the later title/name expansion; `git log -L` traces the helper extraction to 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3. `git cat-file commit 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6` gives the single parent 4ba41a68011c7151925bfcbf3ab6168e97c9d893 and the human-only commit object. Version checks: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 09b1e119^` returns v4.0.0-beta.4, while `git describe --tags --contains 09b1e119` returns v4.0.0-rc.1~32 and tags containing the BIC begin at v4.0.0-rc.1/v4.0.0. The URL-validation guard is absent from v4.14.10 (`git grep` has no match) and present at v4.15.0:src/activitypub/helpers.js:592. The advisory's direct patch c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e adds `if (!Helpers.isUri(tag.icon.url)) return;`; its equivalent branch cherry-pick 7da65694f9934e6f36be0a7f732b22ebc195c6d8 and c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e are both ancestors of release tag v4.15.0 (fbdbb00d01e01a92baf64534a05fd13685cf3d88). Release: https://github.com/NodeBB/NodeBB/releases/tag/v4.15.0.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 makes untrusted ActivityPub emoji metadata executable HTML state: it inserts tag.icon.url into an img attribute and does so before the post is persisted. The direct parent copies content to postData and stores it without any emoji-tag HTML generation, proving immediate-parent absence. The next-day title addition broadens the same already-vulnerable mechanism to tag.name, and the 2026 Helpers.renderEmoji extraction preserves/moves it, so neither later commit displaces the smallest BIC. Tag ancestry places the feature after v4.0.0-beta.4 and in v4.0.0-rc.1 and stable v4.0.0; the vendor guard first appears at the v4.15.0 patched boundary. The referenced c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e is already an atomic direct code fix; 7da65694f9934e6f36be0a7f732b22ebc195c6d8 is an equivalent branch copy, not a distinct root fix. Finally, the only admissible attribution source—the raw 09b1e119 commit object—contains a human author/committer and no AI/bot marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
